source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
DataBank Pittsburgh PIT2 publishes 5 MW of IT capacity across 47,100 square feet of technical space, making it Pennsylvania's second-largest disclosed facility by power, but still a small footprint by AI training standards.

The facility's actual workload density is unknowable from published data. At 40 kW per rack, typical for AI training, 5 MW supports roughly 125 racks. At 10 kW per rack, standard for colocation, it supports around 500 racks. The operator has disclosed neither rack count, power density, nor cooling specification, so whether this campus is configured for high-intensity compute or general-purpose hosting cannot be determined. The absence of published certifications prevents any inference about what workloads qualify for deployment here.

Pennsylvania's total disclosed capacity across mapped facilities is incomplete. Two sites publish megawatt figures totaling 11 MW. Twelve of fourteen mapped facilities publish no capacity data at all. A 5 MW site ranks second in a published sample of two, which indicates meaningful local infrastructure but does not represent the state's true inventory.

This facility's 5 MW capacity is orders of magnitude smaller than single hyperscale AI training deployments. For readers tracking the relationship between grid constraint and AI scaling, a regional facility of this size contributes to local infrastructure but operates at a scale that does not directly compete with the megawatt demands driving power constraint discussions at the national level.
